style: 1997 New York boom bap, 90 BPM, East Coast hardcore hip hop. Male rap vocal: heavyset Brooklyn man in his mid-twenties, deep chest voice, plummy and wheezy, humid breathy tone, thick laid-back grumble with a slight rasp, audible breaths between lines. Calm, unhurried, menacing without raising his voice, every syllable enunciated, sitting right on the beat. Beat: hard dry kick, cracking snare, sparse swung drums, a short dark jazz-piano chord stab looping, vinyl crackle and tape hiss, mono-ish dusty mix, vocal loud and upfront. Between each rule a turntable scratch cuts in a shouted man's voice calling the number. Dark, cold, minimal.
exclude: singing, melodic chorus, autotune, trap hi-hats, 808 bass, synth pads, choir, female vocals, fast double-time flow, shouting rapper, modern polished mix, reverb wash, guitar
lyrics:
[Intro: spoken, low and calm]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Scratch: shouted number cut on the turntable]
[Verse: deep chest voice, unhurried, on the beat]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

[Scratch: shouted number]
Number two: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Scratch: shouted number]
Number three: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Outro: spoken, slow, beat drops out]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[End]
title: tec-r2-chest-voice-literal
